newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse seen flat or falling next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse seen flat or falling next week.

text.p: The Warsaw bourse fell this week and analysts said it was likely to extend losses or stay flat next week as new issues were shifting away funds from the bourse and few positive signals were in sight.

Analysts said that even though the shares were likely to extend Friday's gain on Monday ahead of October earnings reports, due after the close of play on Monday, the market could later drift in a 12,900-14,000 point range.
The main market's all-share WIG index fell 312.1 points or 2.2 percent this week to close at 13,562.7 on Friday.

"I believe we are in a horizontal trend with a downward push and if the market breaks out of the sideways drift it would be rather down than up," said Emil Onyszczuk, a trader at Polish Development Bank (PBR) brokerage.

He added the market could gain significantly only late this month or early in December when about 340 million zlotys of the ten-fold oversubscribed Bank Ochrony Srodowiska (BOS) issue, return to the bourse.
Some analysts, however, expected the market to slide to about 11,5000 points.
They said the rush of firms queueing to tap the market through initial public offerings or new issues was cooling down the market sentiment.
They added some issues, such as rubber producer Stomil Sanok, looked very attractive.

They also said that although the general economic climate remained positive the bourse no longer appeared to be a bargain after a 100-percent growth this year by early October 9 and in the absence of positive signals.
They said, despite the 10.1-percent fall since the October high, the prices still were not attractive enough to draw large capital to the bourse.
Three companies: insurance company TUR Polisa, technical garment maker Lubawa and paper firm Kompap will start bourse trade next week.
Polisa will enter the main market on Wednesday, Lubawa and Kompap the parallel market on Monday and Tuesday respectively.
The week's biggest losers were Remak, which plunged 9.8 percent and Budimex, which fell 8.1 percent.
The top gainers were Irena and Mostostal Warszawa, gaining 5.6 percent each.
